The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Compute Engine** VM that has a high‑end NVIDIA GPU (the closest match to an RTX A6000 that Google offers is the **NVIDIA A100**).  
Both examples assume you already have a project set up (`PROJECT_ID`) and that you have enabled the **Compute Engine API** and the **NVIDIA GPU Driver** package.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI Command

```bash
# Set your project and zone first
export PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
export ZONE="us-central1-a"

# Create a VM named “rtx-a6000-demo” with:
# • 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM (n1-standard-8)
# • 1 NVIDIA A100 GPU
# • Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal)
# • Preemptible (optional – remove if you want a regular instance)
# • Automatic OS login (optional – remove if you prefer key‑based auth)

gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --project=$PROJECT_ID \
    --zone=$ZONE \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=50GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --preemptible \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU (replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with another type if you want a different GPU) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Specifies Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | Disk size & performance |
| `--metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true` | Installs the NVIDIA driver automatically during boot |
| `--preemptible` | Optional – cheaper, but can be terminated after 24h |
| `--tags` | Allows HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules |

> **Note:** If you truly need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to check whether Google Cloud has added that specific GPU model. As of now, the supported GPUs are Tesla T4, P4, P100, V100, and A100.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call (JSON Body)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true" }
    ]
  }
}
```

#### How to send the request

1. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** with scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
   ```bash
   gcloud auth print-access-token
   ```
2. **Send the request** (e.g., using `curl`):

   ```bash
   curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d @instance.json \
     "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances"
   ```

Replace `@instance.json` with the path to a file containing the JSON above.

---

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] Enable **Compute Engine API** in your project.  
- [ ] Ensure you have **billing enabled** and the **GPU quota** for your region.  
- [ ] Verify the GPU type you want is available in your chosen zone (`gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone $ZONE`).  
- [ ] Run the `gcloud` command or POST the JSON payload.  

Once the instance is running, SSH into it and verify the driver installation:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-demo
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the NVIDIA driver version and the A100 GPU listed. Happy computing!
